tickets.title: Strip edges from per-worktree single-ticket .adlc/tickets.json projection (rail enforcement deny-all)
tickets.body:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/voodootikigod/antigravity-booster/issues/11

=== BUG (P0, latent correctness in live rail enforcement) ===
The scheduler materializes each worktree's .adlc/tickets.json as a SINGLE-ticket file: lib/scheduler.mjs (search `writeAdlcTickets(worktree, [planTicketToAdlcTicket(t)])`, ~line 339). planTicketToAdlcTicket (lib/adlc-bridge.mjs ~lines 26-31) preserves `edges` verbatim. For any plan ticket with an outgoing edge (a foundational ticket others depend on), the projected single-ticket file contains an edge whose target is ABSENT from the file. The adlc-antigravity plugin's loadTickets (core-inline.mjs) reports 'edge to unknown ticket <id>'; its railPreconditions treats ANY validation error as tamper and fails closed -> the rails-guard hook denies EVERY structured write (Edit/Write/create_file) for the whole build, not just rail paths. Only leaf tickets (no outgoing edges) enforce correctly, which is why it has been invisible. The only existing test on this path (test/scheduler.test.mjs ~line 339) uses an edge-less ticket.

=== TASK ===
Strip `edges` in the per-worktree single-ticket projection. Rail enforcement only needs id + rails (plus whatever fields the plugin validator requires — check core-inline.mjs validateTicket in the sibling ../adlc/plugins/adlc-antigravity/ checkout for the accepted shape). Do NOT change the repo-level full-set projection written at plan-compile time (lib/adlc-bridge.mjs writeAdlcTickets consumers in lib/plan.mjs) — that file carries the whole DAG and is consumed by the adlc CLI. Implement as an explicit single-ticket variant or an option on the projection helper so the two call sites cannot silently swap.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: New regression test: a plan ticket WITH outgoing edges, projected into a worktree, produces a .adlc/tickets.json with NO edges field (or empty edges) such that a validator applying the plugin's rules (dangling-edge = error) accepts it. The test MUST fail on current main before the fix. VERIFY: run the new test against unfixed code (git stash the fix) and see it fail; then pass with the fix.
- AC2: Repo-level full-set projection unchanged: existing round-trip test in test/adlc-bridge.test.mjs (validates against the real `adlc coldstart` CLI, ~lines 103-138) still green, and full-set projections still carry edges.
- AC3: Full suite green: npm test (127+ tests), fully offline.

Coordination: pairs with adlc repo issue #142 which locks the same contract from the plugin side; the contract decision is: plugin STAYS fail-closed on dangling edges, booster projects edge-free single-ticket files.

edges.contract: lib/scheduler.mjs + lib/adlc-bridge.mjs shared lane; B12 rebases on B11

tickets.title: Plugin contract-version handshake replacing the substring check
tickets.body:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/voodootikigod/antigravity-booster/issues/12

=== PROBLEM (P0, silent version-skew failure mode) ===
The booster's only compatibility check on the installed adlc-antigravity plugin is a substring match: stdout.includes('adlc-antigravity') on `agy plugin list` output (lib/scheduler.mjs ~line 185 in checkEnforcementAvailable, and lib/bootstrap.mjs ~line 64). Nothing verifies the installed plugin speaks the same tickets-schema / hook-payload contract the booster projects. Drift fails silently; worst case is enforcement silently not doing what the booster assumes.

=== TASK ===
1. Booster declares a supported plugin contract (integer or semver range) as a constant in lib/adlc-bridge.mjs (it owns the projected schema).
2. Read the installed plugin manifest at ~/.gemini/config/plugins/adlc-antigravity/plugin.json (make the base dir overridable via env for tests, consistent with existing AGB_* knobs; add the knob to README's env table) and extract its `adlcContract` field (being added by adlc repo issue #143; plugin.json may not carry it yet).
3. checkEnforcementAvailable (lib/scheduler.mjs) and agb bootstrap (lib/bootstrap.mjs): incompatible contract -> abort the run loudly at start BEFORE lock/worktrees with an actionable message (upgrade plugin / upgrade booster). Missing field or unreadable manifest (older plugin) -> warn + degrade exactly as today's enforcement-unavailable path. Never crash: match the repo rule 'CLI integrations degrade, never crash' ({ok:false,error}).

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: Substring check gone from both call sites; manifest-based check in place. VERIFY: grep shows no includes('adlc-antigravity') in lib/scheduler.mjs or lib/bootstrap.mjs used as the compatibility decision.
- AC2: Tests cover: compatible / incompatible / missing-field / unreadable-manifest, in a NEW test file test/handshake.test.mjs via a fixture plugin dir under test/fixtures/ (do NOT touch test/unit.test.mjs — it is in ticket B13's scope). Incompatible aborts before any repo mutation (no lock dir, no .gitignore commit, no worktrees in the fixture target repo).
- AC3: npm test green.

Coordination: soft-depends on adlc repo issue #143 (plugin exposes adlcContract). Land the tolerant reader (missing field = warn+degrade) regardless of #143's merge timing. BLOCKED-BY B11 only via shared files (same lane): build on top of B11's branch or rebase after it merges.

tickets.title: Re-run calibration probes on agy 1.1.1 / engine 2.2.1 and refresh stale doctrine
tickets.body:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/voodootikigod/antigravity-booster/issues/13

=== PROBLEM (P0, scheduler facts are stale) ===
All calibration facts were probed 2026-06-11 on agy 1.0.7 (docs/research/agy-cli.md line 1, docs/calibration/probes-2026-06-11.md). Installed CLI is now 1.1.1; engine 2.2.1 (2026-06-25). Changes plausibly invalidating probed numbers: engine 2.2.1 fixed a subagent deadlock and sandbox-blocking-builtin-skills (both plausibly implicated in the probed ~5m print-mode hard ceiling); agy 1.0.16 added client-side auto-retries on transient errors (changes latency distributions and failure semantics); agy 1.1.1 made print mode return non-zero exit + stderr on server-side failure (probes can now detect failure reliably). GPT-OSS pool cap in lib/pools.mjs (width 2) was set without a full probe.

=== TASK (consumes REAL Antigravity quota — keep probe widths modest, this is measurement not stress-testing) ===
1. Run `agb probe 2,4 <model>` for one representative model per pool (Gemini 3.5 Flash (Medium), Gemini 3.1 Pro (Low), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking), GPT-OSS 120B (Medium)); extend to width 8 ONLY for gemini-flash where the historical degradation claim lives. The probe command appends its artifact to docs/calibration/ automatically.
2. Probe whether the ~5m print ceiling still holds: one prompt designed to exceed 5m with --print-timeout 10m (e.g. instruct a long multi-step generation); record actual wall time and how it terminated.
3. Update lib/pools.mjs POOL_CAPS if measurements moved (or add a dated comment explaining why unchanged).
4. Update stale doctrine text: lib/agy.mjs header comment lines 3-5 ('exits 0 even on print-timeout' is no longer the whole story — 1.1.1 returns non-zero + stderr on server-side failure); add a 'v1.1.1 delta' section to docs/research/agy-cli.md covering: exit codes, --conversation/--continue resume, --agent + agent(s) subcommand, --mode (plan/accept-edits), --project/--new-project, --add-dir, --dangerously-skip-permissions, client auto-retries, permission.allow write allowlisting, agy changelog + plugin validate subcommands.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: New docs/calibration/probes-<today>.md committed with raw measurements (widths, latencies, failures) for all four pools.
- AC2: lib/pools.mjs POOL_CAPS matches the new measurements or carries a dated comment justifying no change.
- AC3: No doc or code comment left claiming agy exit codes are always 0 on failure: grep -ri 'exit 0' lib/ docs/ and reconcile each hit with the 1.1.1 reality.
- AC4: npm test green (POOL_CAPS changes may require updating pool tests).

tickets.title: [P2] feat: append-only events.jsonl for RunStatus
tickets.body:
Implement atomic event logs for the dashboard.

1. Modify `RunStatus` constructor in `lib/status.mjs` to accept `(repo, runId)`. Update `lib/scheduler.mjs` to pass `runId`.
2. Add an `appendEvent(event)` internal function to `RunStatus`. Use a singleton write queue wrapping `await fs.promises.appendFile`. Stringify the event payload synchronously before appending it to the async queue, so rapid mutations to `pools` don't overwrite states. Add a `.catch()` block within the `this.writePromise` chain so that a single write failure doesn't halt the entire run.
3. Modify `status.ticket()` and `status.pools()` to immediately append an event after mutating state. `from` is the `phase` value before the update. `to` maps to `patch.phase`. `detail`, `model`, `strikes` map exactly to `patch`. The `pools` field should just be the raw `this.state.pools` map.
4. Rename `status.finish` to `status.report(summary)`. It continues to write the summary JSON to `.booster/report.json`, but it now also appends a `report` event.
5. Add `status.strike(ticketId, { model, error, strikes })`. It updates state (store `error` directly on the ticket, set `strikes` to the argument, initialize if missing) and flushes to `run.json`, then appends a `strike` event.
6. `.booster/logs/<runId>/events.jsonl` Schema: `{ ts, runId, type: 'phase'|'pool'|'strike'|'report', ticket?, from?, to?, detail?, pools?, model?, error?, done?, report? }`. `ts` is an ISO 8601 string.

Acceptance criteria:
- Replay test dynamically generates events and recreates `run.json` state (merge tickets with `Object.assign`, replace pools).

tickets.title: [P2] feat: normalize transcripts to JSONL
tickets.body:
Normalize per-ticket transcripts to JSONL and update consumers.

1. Normalize per-ticket transcripts to JSONL: one record per agy invocation `{ ts, model, strike, ms, ok, role, error, prompt, output, cwd }`. `role` is mandatory (e.g. 'builder' or 'prosecutor').
2. In `lib/agy.mjs` and `lib/prosecute.mjs`, both builder and prosecutor MUST append to `<ticketId>.jsonl` using `fs.promises.appendFile`.
3. `runAgy` should always write JSONL to `logFile` regardless of the file extension (remove the legacy write branch). `runId` is NOT passed to `runAgy` or `prosecute()`; they receive the exact `logFile` path.
4. In `lib/scheduler.mjs`, change the prosecutor log path passed to `prosecute()` from `<ticketId>.prosecution.jsonl` to `<ticketId>.jsonl`.
5. In `lib/scheduler.mjs` (`checkFlailDetector`), deserialize the JSONL transcript back to raw legacy text using the `role` field to map back correctly. Write it to a temporary file using `crypto.randomUUID()` in `os.tmpdir()` for a unique filename, pass that temp file path to `adlc flail-detector`, and then delete it.
6. Update `docs/usage.md` with semantic descriptions for all fields across `events.jsonl` and `<ticketId>.jsonl`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Transcripts parse as JSONL.
- `test/prosecute.test.mjs` expects JSONL.
- `fake-adlc` keeps working.

tickets.title: [P2] feat: full-screen node TUI dashboard
tickets.body:
Implement zero-dep ANSI TUI inside agb. Use raw ANSI escape sequences to manually place text. DO NOT use blessed or any external dependencies (it is not in package.json).

1. Export an asynchronous `launchTUI(repo, isWatch)` returning `Promise<number | string | undefined>` which resolves to the appropriate exit code or string as handled by `bin/agb.mjs`.
2. Preserve the existing `--ui` flag behavior as expected by `bin/agb.mjs`.
3. Read `.booster/run.json` relative to `repo`. Schema: `runId` at root; `tickets` mapping ticket ID to `{ phase, strikes, model, detail }`; `pools` mapping name to `{ inFlight, cap, requests }`; `done` and `report` at root.
4. TUI layout: 50/50 horizontal width split ratio for the Table vs Gauges vertical panes, and 50/50 horizontal width split ratio for the Timeline vs Transcript tail vertical panes.
5. Ticket table: ID (10 chars), Phase (10 chars), Strikes (3 chars), Model (15 chars). Details maps to `ticket.detail`. Sort alphabetically by ID. Use inverted colors (`{ bg: 'white', fg: 'black' }`) for the selected ticket.
6. Gauges: Sort alphabetically. `[PoolName] [###---] inFlight/cap (requests)`.
7. Timeline: `[ts] {ticketId} strike N: OK` or `[ts] {ticketId} strike N: FAILED - <error>`. `[ts]` is `HH:MM:SS` local time.
8. Transcript tail from `.booster/logs/<runId>/<ticketId>.jsonl`: print `[ts] strike N: <output>`. Truncate output to 1000 characters and append `...` only if exceeded. Strip ANSI sequences via regex before truncating. If file missing, center `Waiting for transcript...` horizontally and vertically.
9. Tail `events.jsonl` using `fs.watch` and `fs.createReadStream` tracking the byte offset. Buffer incoming stream chunks until a newline (`\n`) is encountered, or use the `readline` module, before attempting to parse the JSON.
10. Explicitly call `watcher.close()` and `stream.destroy()` on the active transcript file before opening a new one during navigation.
11. Wait for `q` to quit (resolving Promise with undefined). Restore raw mode on exit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Live run renders all panes.
- Pure render functions unit-tested.
- Exactly zero dependencies.

tickets.title: Evaluate Linux sandbox functionality for Ubuntu
tickets.body:
Evaluate ways to bring the macOS sandbox functionality to Ubuntu Linux. Research mechanisms like AppArmor, seccomp, bwrap (Bubblewrap), or Firejail that provide analogous capabilities to the macOS sandbox profile. The goal is to achieve similar operational ease and security benefits for the Antigravity toolkit. Document the findings, trade-offs, and a proposed implementation plan in docs/research/linux-sandbox.md.

Implementation Decisions:
- Adopt `bubblewrap` (`bwrap`) as the Linux sandbox engine.
- Fail closed if `bwrap` is missing on Linux (instruct user to `apt install bubblewrap` or use `AGB_SANDBOX_GATES=0`).
- Catch execution failures specific to unprivileged user namespaces and provide actionable errors with fixes.
- Install `bubblewrap` in Ubuntu CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and enable `test/security.test.mjs` on Linux.
